confirm.text: Four forms carry an "Unsafe conditions" selection in the "What did we observe?" multi-select. None of the 28 air job forms reviewed selected "Stop work authority utilized" — every form that mentions stop-work authority at all selected "Stop work authority was discussed", which is a routine pre-job item and not a stop-work event. These are listed so the technicians can confirm what they meant, not as confirmed events.
Forms selecting "Unsafe conditions" together with "Stop work authority was discussed":

Ruben Rojo — XTO, XBC Giddings 1015, 2:38 PM, job 37105_1. The narrative describes routine work: "Disconnect of old parts and replacement of said old ones with new lines to wellhead" and "With pumpers and pump trucks present there was no signs of gas or other hazardous materials before and after break". No specific unsafe condition is named anywhere on the form.
1099 Robert Henigan — XTO, Cox-Carlos 19A 1H, 10:10 AM, job 37000. Narrative reads "Disconnect", "Everything" and "Job went well no issues". No unsafe condition is named.

1099 William Jimmy Cooper — XTO, Nail Tillman E1J 510H, 10:44 AM, job 37068. Narrative reads "Lines removed from well head prep for work over" and "Job completed with out incident". No unsafe condition is named.
1099 William Jimmy Cooper — XTO, Scharbauer Ranch #1605, 11:40 AM, job 37072. See below.

Cooper's Scharbauer Ranch form is not the ordinary mis-selection pattern and should be looked at separately. Both technicians on that location recorded that the job could not be performed — Cooper's "Details if Any" reads "Work over rig over hole unable to preform job" and Ralph Forbes's form for the same ticket reads "Pulling unit on well next to job. Job will be rescheduled". Cooper's form nonetheless carries the full ten-item observation multi-select including "Unsafe conditions", with "What Did We Observe? Continued: NA", an empty "What went well?" multi-select and a Learn section of "NA". A complete observation set on a job that did not happen points to the selection being carried forward rather than made fresh, which is the training point Kelby raised on 09/23. It is also possible a genuine condition — a workover rig sitting over the hole next to the work area — is what prompted it

The identical nine-item observation string appears verbatim on six separate forms today (Sanders 36898 and 36910, Henigan 37098_2, Forbes 37067, Jobe 36996 and Cooper 37068), which is the same carry-forward pattern. Looking across previous days: 1099 William Jimmy Cooper appears on this list twice today, Michael Jobe — who selected "Unsafe conditions" twice without supporting narrative on 09/26 — was clear again today, and Nathan Contreras and Jose Campos filed nothing today. No form today named a real condition in the narrative while leaving "Unsafe conditions" unselected.

Trailer Inspection Forms, Trailer Readiness Forms and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based, so a defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images and not as text, so they cannot be checked here — Tyrell Sanders's extinguisher tag surfaced only because he typed a note about it. Where a photo label appears with no capture attached, as on 1099 Gage Gonzales's Loud Alarm Position and back-of-trailer photos and on several Trailer Readiness Forms, this review can say the capture is absent from the record but not whether the equipment was there.

93 of 93 submissions read. The job board was available — Blake Walton's 11/17/2026 boards arrived at 10:05 AM Central and both the ArkLaTex and Permian Basin workbooks were used, with 50 manned rows checked for coverage (41 WTX, 9 ETX). This run started at 11:06 PM Central, before the Central day closed, so any form submitted in the last hour of 11/17 is not in these counts; a missing Trailer Readiness Form is the finding most often resolved by a late submission, and none was outstanding tonight.
